plan: Isaiah 12:1-6; Isaiah 17:1-14; 2 Chronicles 28:16-21; 2 Kings 16:10-18; 2 Chronicles 28:22-25; 2 Kings 18:1-8; 2 Chronicles 29:1-2; 2 Kings 15:30-31; 2 Kings 17:1-4; Hosea 1:1, 2–2:1; Hosea 2:2-13

readings.title: A Song of Thanksgiving
readings.subtitle: Praise for YeHoVaH's Deliverance
readings.text:
[Isaiah 12:1] And in that day you shall say, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> thank <dn>You</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, though <dn>You</dn> were enraged with me, <dn>Your</dn> displeasure has turned back, and <dn>You</dn> have comforted me.</dq>
[2] <dq>“See, <dn>Ěl</dn> is my deliverance, <dn>I</dn> trust and am not afraid. For Yah, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, is my strength and my song; and <dn>He</dn> has become my deliverance.”</dq>
[3] And you shall draw water with joy from the fountains of deliverance.
[4] And in that day you shall say, <dq>“Praise <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, call upon <dn>His</dn> Name; make known <dn>His</dn> deeds among the peoples, make mention that <dn>His</dn> Name is exalted.</dq>
[5] <dq>“Sing to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, For <dn>He</dn> has done excellently; this is known in all the earth.</dq>
[6] <dq>"Cry aloud and shout, O inhabitant of Tsiyon, for great is the Set-apart One of Yisra’ěl in your midst!”</dq>

readings.title: The Message Concerning Damascus
readings.subtitle: The Ruin of Aram and Ephraim
readings.text:
[Isaiah 17:1] The message concerning Dammeseq. <dq>“See, Dammeseq ceases to be a city, and shall become a heap of ruins.</dq>
[2] <dq>“The cities of Aro‛ěr are forsaken, they are for flocks which shall lie down, with no one to frighten.</dq>
[3] <dq>“And the stronghold shall cease from Ephrayim, and the reign from Dammeseq, and the remnant of Aram be as the esteem of the sons of Yisra’ěl,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts.
[4] <dq>“And in that day it shall be that the esteem of Ya‛aqoḇ wanes, and the fatness of his flesh grows lean.</dq>
[5] <dq>“And it shall be as when the harvester gathers the grain, and reaps the heads with his arm. And it shall be as he who gathers heads of grain in the Valley of Repha’im.</dq>
[6] <dq>“And gleaning grapes shall be left in it, like the shaking of an olive tree, two or three olives at the top of the uppermost branch, four or five in its most fruit-bearing branches,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl.
[7] In that day man shall look to his Maker, and his eyes turn to the Set-apart One of Yisra’ěl.
[8] And he shall not look to the slaughter-places, the work of his hands; and he shall not see that which his own fingers made, nor the Ashěrim nor the sun-pillars.
[9] In that day his strong cities become like a forsaken forest and an uppermost branch, which they left because of the children of Yisra’ěl. And it shall become a ruin.

readings.title: The Consequence of Forgetting Elohim
readings.subtitle: The Swift Destruction of Israel's Foes
readings.text:
[Isaiah 17:10] Because you have forgotten <dn>את</dn> the <dn>Elohim</dn> of your deliverance, and have not remembered the Rock of your stronghold, therefore you shall plant pleasant plants and set out foreign seedlings,
[11] by day make your plant to grow, and in the morning make your seed to flourish – but the harvest is a heap in the day of grief and incurable pain.
[12] Woe to the uproar of many people who make a noise like the roar of the seas, and to the rushing of nations that make a rushing like the rushing of mighty waters –
[13] nations rushing like the rushing of many waters. But <dn>He</dn> shall rebuke them and they shall flee far away, and be chased like the chaff of the mountains before the wind, like whirling dust before the whirlwind.
[14] At eventide, look! Alarm! Before morning, it is no more. This is the portion of those who plunder us, and the lot of those who rob us.

readings.subsection: The Reign of Ahaz in Judah
readings.title: Ahaz's Idolatrous Altar
readings.subtitle: The King Desecrates the Temple
readings.text:
[2 Kings 16:10] And Sovereign Aḥaz went to meet Tiḡlath-Pileser sovereign of Ashshur at Dammeseq, and saw a slaughter-place that was at Dammeseq. And Sovereign Aḥaz sent to Uriyah the priest a sketch of the slaughter-place and its pattern, according to all its workmanship.
[11] And Uriyah the priest built a slaughter-place according to all that Sovereign Aḥaz had sent from Dammeseq. And Uriyah the priest made it before Sovereign Aḥaz came from Dammeseq.
[12] And when the sovereign came from Dammeseq, the sovereign saw the slaughter-place, and the sovereign approached the slaughter-place and made offerings on it.
[13] And he burned his ascending offering and his grain offering. And he poured his drink offering and sprinkled the blood of his peace offerings on the slaughter-place.
[14] And <dn>את</dn> the bronze slaughter-place which was before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> he brought from the front of the House, from between the new slaughter-place and the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and put it on the north side of his slaughter-place.
[15] And Sovereign Aḥaz commanded Uriyah the priest, saying, “On the great slaughter-place burn the morning ascending offering, and the evening grain offering, and the sovereign’s ascending offering, and his grain offering, with the ascending offering of all the people of the land, and their grain offering, and their drink offerings. And sprinkle on it <dn>את</dn> all the blood of the ascending offering and <dn>את</dn> all the blood of the slaughtering. And the bronze slaughter-place is for me to inquire by.”
[16] And Uriyah the priest did according to all that Sovereign Aḥaz commanded.
[17] And Sovereign Aḥaz cut off <dn>את</dn> the side panels of the stands, and removed <dn>את</dn> the basins from them. And he took down <dn>את</dn> the Sea from the bronze oxen that were under it, and put it on a pavement of stones.
[18] And <dn>את</dn> the covered way which they had built in the House for the Sabbath, and <dn>את</dn> the sovereign’s outer entrance, he took from the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, because of the sovereign of Ashshur.

readings.subsection: The Reign of Hezekiah in Judah
readings.title: Hezekiah's Righteous Reign
readings.subtitle: Reforms and Rebellion Against Assyria
readings.text:
[2 Kings 18:1] And it came to be in the third year of Hoshěa son of Ělah, sovereign of Yisra’ěl, that Ḥizqiyah son of Aḥaz, sovereign of Yehuḏah, began to reign.
[2] He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Yerushalayim. And his mother’s name was Aḇi, daughter of Zeḵaryah.
[3] And he did what was right in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, according to all that his father Daviḏ did.
[4] He took away <dn>את</dn> the high places and broke <dn>את</dn> the pillars, and cut down <dn>את</dn> the Ashěrah, and broke in pieces <dn>את</dn> the bronze serpent which Mosheh had made, for until those days the children of Yisra’ěl burned incense to it, and called it Neḥushtan.
[5] He put his trust in <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, and after him was none like him among all the sovereigns of Yehuḏah, nor who were before him,
[6] and he clung to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. He did not turn away from following <dn>Him</dn>, but guarded <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> commands, which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded <dn>את</dn> Mosheh.
[7] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was with him – wherever he went he acted wisely. And he rebelled against the sovereign of Ashshur and did not serve him.
[8] He struck <dn>את</dn> the Philistines, as far as Azzah and its borders – from watchtower unto the walled city.

readings.subsection: The Decline of the Northern Kingdom
readings.title: Hoshea Assassinates Pekah
readings.subtitle: The End of Pekah's Reign in Israel
readings.text:
[2 Kings 15:30] And Hoshěa son of Ělah led a conspiracy against Peqaḥ son of Remalyahu, and struck <dn>את</dn> him, and killed him, and reigned in his place in the twentieth year of Yotham son of Uzziyah.
[31] And the rest of the acts of Peqaḥ, and all that he did, see, they are written in the book of the annals of the sovereigns of Yisra’ěl.

readings.subsection: The Fall of the Northern Kingdom
readings.title: Hoshea, Last King of Israel
readings.subtitle: Vassalage and Conspiracy Against Assyria
readings.text:
[2 Kings 17:1] In the twelfth year of Aḥaz sovereign of Yehuḏah, Hoshěa son of Ělah began to reign over Yisra’ěl in Shomeron, for nine years.
[2] And he did evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, but not as the sovereigns of Yisra’ěl who were before him.
[3] Shalmaneser sovereign of Ashshur came up against him. And Hoshěa became his servant, and rendered him <dn>את</dn> a present.
[4] But the sovereign of Ashshur found a conspiracy in Hoshěa, for he had sent messengers to So, sovereign of Mitsrayim, and had not brought a present to the sovereign of Ashshur, as year by year. And the sovereign of Ashshur shut him up, and bound him in prison.

readings.title: Hosea's Marriage to Gomer
readings.subtitle: Children of Whoredom as a Sign
readings.text:
[Hosea 1:1] The word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> that came to Hoshěa son of Be’ěri, in the days of Uzziyah, Yotham, Aḥaz, and Yeḥizqiyah, sovereigns of Yehuḏah, and in the days of Yaroḇ‛am son of Yo’ash, sovereign of Yisra’ěl.
[2] The beginning of the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> with Hoshěa. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Hoshěa, <dq>“Go, take yourself <dn>את</dn> a woman of whoring and <dn>את</dn> children of whoring, for the land has utterly whored away from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.”</dq>
[3] So he went and took Gomer, daughter of Diḇlayim, and she conceived and bore him a son.
[4] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to him, <dq>“Call his name Yizre‛ěl, for in a little while <dn>I</dn> shall revenge <dn>את</dn> the bloodshed of Yizre‛ěl on the house of Yěhu, and put an end to <dn>את</dn> the reign of the house of Yisra’ěl.</dq>
[5] <dq>“And it shall be in that day that <dn>I</dn> shall break <dn>את</dn> the bow of Yisra’ěl in the Valley of Yizre‛ěl.”</dq>
[6] And she conceived again and bore a daughter. And <dn>He</dn> said to him, <dq>“Call her name Lo-Ruḥamah, for no longer do <dn>I</dn> have compassion on <dn>את</dn> the house of Yisra’ěl so as to forgive them at all.</dq>
[7] <dq>“But <dn>I</dn> shall have compassion on <dn>את</dn> the house of Yehuḏah and save <dn>את</dn> them by <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> their <dn>Elohim</dn>, and not save them by bow or by sword or battle, by horses or horsemen.”</dq>
[8] And she weaned Lo-Ruḥamah, and conceived and bore a son,
[9] then <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“Call his name Lo-Ammi, for you are not <dn>My</dn> people, and <dn>I</dn> am not for you.</dq>

readings.title: Promise of Restoration
readings.subtitle: Not My People Will Be Called Sons of the Living El
readings.text:
[Hosea 1:10] <dq>“Yet the number of the children of Yisra’ěl shall be as the sand of the sea, which is not measured nor counted. And it shall be in the place where it was said to them, ‘You are not <dn>My</dn> people,’ they shall be called, ‘You are the sons of the living <dn>Ěl</dn>.’</dq>
[11] <dq>“And the children of Yehuḏah and the children of Yisra’ěl shall be gathered together, and appoint for themselves one head, and shall come up out of the earth, for great is the day of Yizre‛ěl!</dq>
[Hosea 2:1] <dq>“Say to your brothers, ‘O my people,’ and to your sisters, ‘O, compassioned one.’</dq>

readings.title: The Charge Against Unfaithful Israel
readings.subtitle: Consequences of Idolatry and Forgetting YeHoVaH
readings.text:
[Hosea 2:2] <dq>“Strive with your mother, strive, for she is not <dn>My</dn> wife, nor am <dn>I</dn> her Husband! Let her put away <dn>את</dn> her whorings from her face, and <dn>את</dn> her adulteries from between her breasts,</dq>
[3] <dq>lest <dn>I</dn> strip her naked, and shall set her up as on the day she was born, and shall make her like a wilderness, and shall set her like a dry land, and shall put her to death with thirst.</dq>
[4] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall not have compassion on her children, for they are the children of whorings.</dq>
[5] <dq>“For their mother has whored, she who conceived them has acted shamelessly. For she said, ‘<dn>I</dn> go after my lovers, who give me my bread and my water, my wool and my linen, my oil and my drink.’</dq>
[6] <dq>“Therefore, see, <dn>I</dn> am hedging up your way with thorns, and <dn>I</dn> shall wall her in, so that she does not find her paths.</dq>
[7] <dq>“And she shall pursue her lovers but not overtake them, and shall seek them but not find them. Then she shall say, ‘Let me go and return to my first husband, for then it was better for me than now.’</dq>
[8] <dq>“And she did not acknowledge that <dn>I</dn> gave her grain, and new wine, and oil, and increased her silver and gold which they prepared for Ba‛al.</dq>
[9] <dq>“Therefore <dn>I</dn> shall turn back and shall take <dn>My</dn> grain in its time and <dn>My</dn> new wine in its appointed time, and <dn>I</dn> shall take away <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> wool and <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> linen covering her nakedness.</dq>
[10] <dq>“And now <dn>I</dn> shall uncover her shame before the eyes of her lovers, and no one shall deliver her from <dn>My</dn> hand.</dq>
[11] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall cause all her rejoicing, her festivals, her New moons, and her Sabbaths, even all her appointed times, to cease,</dq>
[12] <dq>and lay waste <dn>את</dn> her vines and <dn>את</dn> her fig trees, of which she has said, ‘these are my harlot-fees that my lovers have given me.’ And <dn>I</dn> shall make them a forest, and the beasts of the field shall eat them.</dq>
[13] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall punish her for the days of the Ba‛als to which she burned incense and adorned herself with her rings and jewelry, and went after her lovers, and forgot <dn>את</dn> <dn>Me</dn>,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
